title: Matthew Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 9.

questions.question: What city did Jesus come into after passing over in a ship?
questions.explanation: Jesus entered into His own city as stated in Matthew 9:1.

questions.question: What condition did the man brought to Jesus suffer from?
questions.explanation: The man was sick of the palsy, as noted in Matthew 9:2.

questions.question: Who questioned Jesus' authority to forgive sins?
questions.explanation: Certain scribes said within themselves that Jesus blasphemeth, as mentioned in Matthew 9:3.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the sick of the palsy that his sins were forgiven.
questions.explanation: Jesus said unto the sick of the palsy, 'Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee' (Matthew 9:2).

questions.question: What did Jesus ask the scribes regarding their thoughts?
options: Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
Who are you to question me?
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
questions.explanation: Jesus knew their thoughts and asked them this question in Matthew 9:4.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said it is easier to say 'Thy sins be forgiven thee' than to say 'Arise, and walk.'
questions.explanation: Jesus posed this question to illustrate His authority, stating it is easier to say 'Thy sins be forgiven thee' (Matthew 9:5).

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the sick of the palsy to do after forgiving his sins?
options: Take up thy bed and walk
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded the sick of the palsy to arise and go home after forgiving his sins (Matthew 9:6).

questions.question: True or False: The multitudes glorified God after witnessing Jesus' miracle.
questions.explanation: The multitudes marvelled and glorified God after seeing the miracle performed by Jesus (Matthew 9:8).

questions.question: Who did Jesus call to follow him while sitting at the receipt of custom?
questions.explanation: Jesus saw a man named Matthew and called him to follow in Matthew 9:9.

questions.question: What reason did the Pharisees give for questioning Jesus' actions?
options: He ate with publicans and sinners
He claimed to be the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: He ate with publicans and sinners
questions.explanation: The Pharisees questioned why Jesus ate with publicans and sinners (Matthew 9:11).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus came to call the righteous to repentance.
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that He did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance (Matthew 9:13).

questions.question: In what order did Jesus perform the miracle of healing the man sick of the palsy?
options: He forgave his sins, then healed him
He healed him, then forgave his sins
He told him to follow him
questions.correctAnswer: He forgave his sins, then healed him
questions.explanation: Jesus first forgave the man's sins before healing him, as described in Matthew 9:2-6.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the man sick of the palsy before healing him?
questions.explanation: Jesus first addressed the man's spiritual need by saying, 'Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.' (Matthew 9:2). This shows the importance of faith and forgiveness.

questions.question: Why did the Pharisees question Jesus about eating with publicans and sinners?
options: They wanted to learn from Him
They were jealous of His popularity
questions.explanation: The Pharisees questioned His disciples, saying, 'Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?' indicating they believed it was inappropriate for Jesus to associate with them. (Matthew 9:11).

questions.question: According to Jesus, who needs a physician?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated, 'They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.' (Matthew 9:12). This illustrates the need for spiritual healing among those who recognize their sinfulness.

questions.question: What teaching does Jesus give about fasting when He is present?
options: They cannot mourn while the bridegroom is with them
questions.correctAnswer: They cannot mourn while the bridegroom is with them
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that 'Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them?' (Matthew 9:15), indicating that His presence brings joy.

questions.question: What analogy does Jesus use to explain the need for new practices?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches, 'Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break.' (Matthew 9:17). This emphasizes the need for new approaches in His ministry.

questions.question: What did the woman with the issue of blood believe would make her whole?
questions.explanation: The woman said, 'If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.' (Matthew 9:21), demonstrating her strong faith in Jesus' power to heal.

questions.question: What was the response of the people when Jesus said the maid was not dead?
questions.explanation: When Jesus said, 'the maid is not dead, but sleepeth,' the people laughed Him to scorn (Matthew 9:24), showing their disbelief in His power.

questions.question: What did Jesus do before raising the maid from the dead?
options: He commanded the people to leave
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded the people to leave
questions.explanation: Jesus told the people, 'Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth,' and when they laughed, He put them forth before healing her. (Matthew 9:24).

questions.question: What did the two blind men call Jesus?
questions.explanation: The blind men followed Him, crying, 'Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.' (Matthew 9:27), acknowledging His messianic lineage.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the blind men to keep their healing a secret.
questions.explanation: After healing the blind men, Jesus 'straitly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.' (Matthew 9:30), indicating He wanted to manage the spread of His fame.

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees believed Jesus cast out devils by the power of God.
questions.explanation: The Pharisees accused Jesus of casting out devils through the prince of the devils, showing their skepticism about His authority. (Matthew 9:34).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was moved with compassion when He saw the multitudes.
questions.explanation: When Jesus saw the multitudes, 'he was moved with compassion on them' because they were like sheep without a shepherd. (Matthew 9:36).

questions.question: What does Matthew 9:37 teach about the state of the harvest?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated, 'The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.' (Matthew 9:37), indicating a great need for workers in spreading the Gospel.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 9.

questions.question: What did the two blind men call Jesus as they followed him?
questions.explanation: The two blind men cried out to Jesus, calling him 'Thou Son of David,' which signifies their recognition of him as the Messiah, fulfilling the prophecy of a descendant of David (Matthew 9:27).

questions.question: According to Jesus, what is the connection between faith and healing?
options: According to your faith be it unto you
Healing is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: According to your faith be it unto you
questions.explanation: Jesus told the blind men, 'According to your faith be it unto you,' indicating that their healing was directly related to their faith (Matthew 9:29).

questions.question: What did the Pharisees accuse Jesus of when he cast out demons?
options: He heals by the power of God
He casts out devils through the prince of devils
questions.correctAnswer: He casts out devils through the prince of devils
questions.explanation: The Pharisees claimed that Jesus cast out demons by the power of Beelzebub, showing their disbelief in him (Matthew 9:34).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the harvest and the laborers?
options: The harvest is plenteous, but the laborers are few
The harvest is plentiful and easy
questions.correctAnswer: The harvest is plenteous, but the laborers are few
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that 'The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few,' emphasizing the need for more workers in God's mission (Matthew 9:37).

questions.question: Which act of healing did Jesus perform that surprised the multitudes?
options: He cured a woman with a fever
He raised a girl from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: He raised a girl from the dead
questions.explanation: Jesus raised the ruler's daughter from the dead, which caused the multitudes to marvel at his power (Matthew 9:25).

questions.question: What was the condition of the woman who touched Jesus' garment?
options: She had an issue of blood for twelve years
questions.correctAnswer: She had an issue of blood for twelve years
questions.explanation: The woman had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years before she touched Jesus' garment and was healed (Matthew 9:20-21).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Matthew 9:36 when Jesus sees the multitudes?
questions.explanation: The metaphor of sheep having no shepherd illustrates the people's lack of guidance and care, paralleling Old Testament themes (Matthew 9:36).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus commanded the blind men to keep their healing a secret.
questions.explanation: Jesus charged the blind men to not let anyone know about their healing, indicating a desire to manage his fame (Matthew 9:30).

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he said, 'They that be whole need not a physician'?
options: Healthy people do not need help
Only the righteous can be healed
questions.explanation: Jesus was indicating that he came to heal sinners, not the righteous, highlighting his mission to save the lost (Matthew 9:12-13).

questions.question: According to Matthew 9:35, what three activities did Jesus engage in during his ministry?
questions.explanation: Jesus went about teaching in synagogues, preaching the gospel, and healing every sickness, summarizing his ministry (Matthew 9:35).

questions.question: True or False: The fame of Jesus spread only after he raised the ruler's daughter.
questions.explanation: The fame of Jesus spread after various miracles, including the healing of the blind men and the woman with the issue of blood, not solely after raising the ruler's daughter (Matthew 9:31).

questions.question: In the context of Matthew 9, what does the phrase 'the bridegroom shall be taken from them' symbolize?
questions.explanation: This phrase foreshadows Jesus' own death and the resulting sorrow of his disciples, marking a significant change in their relationship (Matthew 9:15).

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy relates to the healing of the woman with the issue of blood?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of the Messiah bearing our infirmities, which is fulfilled in Jesus' healing ministry, including the woman's healing (Matthew 9:20-22).

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jesus declare to the man sick of the palsy before healing him?
options: Thy faith hath made thee whole
questions.explanation: Jesus first tells the man sick of the palsy that his sins are forgiven, demonstrating His authority to forgive sins (Matthew 9:2).

questions.question: What did the multitudes do when they saw the healing of the sick of the palsy?
questions.explanation: The multitudes marveled and glorified God for the power He had given unto men, as seen in Matthew 9:8.

questions.question: What role does Jesus say the sick play in relation to a physician?
options: Only the righteous need a physician
The whole need not a physician
Only the healed need a physician
questions.correctAnswer: The whole need not a physician
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that those who are whole do not need a physician, but those who are sick do, highlighting the need for repentance and healing (Matthew 9:12).

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by saying He came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance?
options: He offers mercy to the unrepentant
He prioritizes the sick over the healthy
He came to fulfill the law
questions.correctAnswer: He offers mercy to the unrepentant
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes His mission to offer mercy and call sinners to repentance, which signifies His role in salvation (Matthew 9:13).

questions.question: What does Jesus compare putting new cloth on an old garment to?
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the analogy of new cloth and old garments to illustrate the incompatibility of new teachings with old traditions (Matthew 9:16).

questions.question: What does the healing of the ruler's daughter symbolize in the context of Jesus' ministry?
questions.explanation: The healing of the ruler's daughter shows Jesus' divine authority over life and death, a key aspect of His messianic identity (Matthew 9:25).

questions.question: What does the woman with the issue of blood believe will heal her?
questions.explanation: The woman believed that touching the hem of Jesus' garment would make her whole, demonstrating her faith in His healing power (Matthew 9:21).

questions.question: How does Jesus respond to the blind men who seek His mercy?
options: He asks if they believe He can heal them
He says they are not ready
questions.correctAnswer: He asks if they believe He can heal them
questions.explanation: Jesus' question to the blind men emphasizes the importance of faith in receiving healing (Matthew 9:28).

questions.question: What claim do the Pharisees make about Jesus casting out devils?
options: He does it by the Spirit of God
He does it through the prince of devils
He does it with the help of the disciples
He does it at the request of the sick
questions.correctAnswer: He does it through the prince of devils
questions.explanation: The Pharisees accused Jesus of casting out devils by the power of Beelzebub, challenging His authority (Matthew 9:34).

questions.question: What does Jesus do in all the cities and villages according to this chapter?
options: He teaches and preaches the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: He teaches and preaches the gospel
questions.explanation: Jesus goes about teaching in synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, fulfilling His mission (Matthew 9:35).

questions.question: What does Jesus feel toward the multitudes when He sees them scattered?
questions.explanation: Jesus is moved with compassion for the multitudes, recognizing their spiritual need, which reflects His loving character (Matthew 9:36).

questions.question: What does Jesus instruct His disciples to pray for?
questions.explanation: Jesus tells His disciples to pray for laborers to be sent into the harvest, emphasizing the need for workers in the ministry (Matthew 9:38).

questions.question: What does the healing of the dumb man signify in relation to Jesus' authority?
questions.explanation: The healing of the dumb man possessed by a devil highlights Jesus' authority over demonic forces (Matthew 9:33).

questions.question: What did the disciples of John question Jesus about?
options: Why He heals on the Sabbath
Why His disciples do not fast
questions.correctAnswer: Why His disciples do not fast
questions.explanation: The disciples of John asked why Jesus' disciples do not fast, highlighting a contrast in spiritual practices (Matthew 9:14).

questions.question: What does Jesus compare the situation of mourning to when He is present?
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the analogy of a wedding feast to explain that His presence brings joy, contrasting it with the sadness of fasting (Matthew 9:15).
